title: Affinity flapping detection and fast remediation cheatsheet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, practical cheatsheet for oncall SREs to detect, confirm, and quickly remediate affinity/anti-affinity flapping and tenant-driven oscillations in Dedicated GPU pools. Focus is on fast, reversible actions that restore latency and throughput while minimizing blast radius.

When to use this doc:
- Sudden throughput drop with stable infra health metrics (CPU/GPU utilization unchanged but request latency jumps)
- Repeated small-scale reassignments of slots to tenants in a short window (minutes)
- Autoscaler thrash: pools scale up/down rapidly without sustained load change
- Spike in per-tenant eviction or bind failures

Quick detection checklist (0-7 min):
1) Signal summary (first 60s):
   - Check router/ingress 5xx/timeout spike (gateway logs). Start Slack thread, ping oncall rotations.
   - Pager fields: top-5 tenants by 95th latency and by request-rate.
2) PromQL / metric sanity checks (use grafana explore):
   - Tenanted eviction rate: sum by(tenant) (increase(rate(allocator_evictions_total[2m])) )
   - Pod bind churn: increase(kube_scheduled_pods_total[2m]) or custom: increase(allocator_bind_ops_total[2m])
   - Pool-level throttling: rate(gpu_scheduler_backpressure_total[1m]) > 0. See if correlated to tenant_id tag.
   - KV cache misses amplification: rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m]) per-tenant
3) Quick logs commands (kubectl / allocator CLI):
   - allocator: ./bin/allocator inspect-pool --pool dedicated-eu-west-1a | jq '.tenants | sort_by(.evictions) | reverse | .[0:8]'
   - kubectl -n allocator logs deploy/allocator --since=10m | grep tenant_id | tail -n 200
   - dmesg / driver logs only if GPU thermal or firmware events show up (rare).
4) Heatmap: check cross-tenant affinity score over last 30m. Look for rapid flips (affinity score crossing pinned threshold repeatedly).

Immediate mitigations (fast, reversible)
- If a single tenant is high-churn and clearly the cause: throttle tenant (rate limit) or put tenant into soft-evict state to drain long-running sessions. Commands: allocator patch-tenant --id T-123 --max-concurrency 8 --throttle 50%
- Cordon suspect nodes: kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-17 && drain with --ignore-daemonsets if safe. This prevents noisy placement while migrations/evictions settle.
- Toggle affinity enforcement to 'soft' for the affected pool: POST /admin/pools/dedicated-eu-west-1a/affinity?mode=soft
- Increase autoscaler hysteresis temporarily: set min-scale-delay=300s, cooldown-window=600s to stop oscillation.
- Apply emergency fallback: route a small % (5-10%) of traffic to regional fallback pool (lower capacity but stable) via routing policy.

Order of operations (recommended oncall flow):
1) Confirm signal and start comms (Slack + incident channel). Attach top-3 Prometheus graphs.
2) Identify top-3 suspected tenants and run inspect/pool and binder logs.
3) If >1 tenant flapping -> likely scheduler or autoscaler policy. Increase autoscaler hysteresis and pause scale actions for 2min.
4) If single tenant == culprit -> throttle and document tenant ID, contact SE/Account if customer-visible.
5) If node-level instability suspected (driver errors/thermal) -> cordon node and migrate workloads.
6) Re-evaluate after each step (wait 2–3 minutes for metrics to reflect).

Detection heuristics and thresholds (for alerts / playbooks):
- Eviction spike: > 5 evictions/min for a single tenant over a 3-minute window.
- Churn ratio: (bind_ops + unbind_ops) / successful_allocations > 0.2 sustained for 5m => flapping candidate.
- Autoscaler oscillation: pool size changed >=2 times within 10m with <20% change in request-rate.
- KV amplification: per-tenant kv_cache_miss rate increase > 3x baseline and correlates to burst of short-lived sessions.

Common root causes (fast map):
- Noisy client behavior: tiny repeated sessions, poor keepalive, frequent reconnects.
- Misconfigured affinity/anti-affinity thresholds or an aggressive hard-affinity rollout.
- Autoscaler parameters too tight (short cooldown/hysteresis).
- Bug in allocator that reroutes on transient error (see linked PR).
- Resource pressure from bursty batch jobs that bypass per-tenant controls.

Communication templates (Slack / incident notes):
- Initial post:
  "SRE oncall: Investigating CPU/GPU latency spike in dedicated-eu-west-1a. Observed eviction churn and scheduler bind thrash. Collecting top-3 tenants and will post mitigation in 10m. Pager: @eng-sre @allocator-team"
- Customer-facing (for support handoff):
  "We observed elevated request latency for your workload between 15:12–15:38 UTC due to cluster placement churn. We applied a temporary throttle and increased autoscale cooldown; we'll follow up with a root-cause update by EOD. (Incident ref: JIRA-1234)"

Notes to oncall (gotchas / heuristics):
- Don’t immediately restart allocator if you can throttle and stabilize; restarts cause additional binds.
- When cordoning, prefer draining only the suspect tenant's pods (if possible) to avoid global migrations.
- Watch for prefix cache warming: after mitigation you may see transient higher latency while caches rebuild. This is expected; track kv_cache_hit_ratio.

Short post-incident checklist (first 24h):
- Owner: oncall that handled incident -> create postmortem draft and link JIRA.
- Run heap/profile on allocator if allocator logs show repeated reroutes (assign to eng/serving-runtime).
- Add short-term alert: new alert for churn ratio described above (eng-sre).
- Patch autoscaler defaults: increase default cooldown to 5m and hysteresis to conservative values (eng-platform).
- Customer outreach: CS + SE to notify affected customers and optionally offer credits (CS lead).

Longer-term follow-ups (next sprint):
- Add tenancy-level rate-limiting enforcement in allocator control plane (product + eng).
- Improve affinity rollout: gradual ramp with health probes before hard-affinity enforcement.
- Simulate noisy-tenant scenarios in chaos lab to measure tolerance and tune autoscaler.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we include tenant session-length percentiles in SLO dashboard? (Priya to prototype)
- Can allocator expose per-tenant historical affinity flip counts? Might need a small counter metric.
- Determine safe default for soft-affinity window: 2m vs 5m.

Appendix: useful one-liners
- Quick top-ten tenants by evictions (allocator CLI):
  ./bin/allocator top-evictions --pool dedicated-eu-west-1a --window 10m | head -n 10
- Temporarily pause autoscaler: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/pools/dedicated-eu-west-1a/autoscaler/pause?reason=incident
- Re-enable affinity soft-mode: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/admin/pools/affinity -d '{"pool":"dedicated-eu-west-1a","mode":"soft"}'

Last updated notes:
- 2026-02-01: initial draft with detection heuristics and quick actions.
- 2026-03-01: added throttling command syntaxes and comms templates; linked JIRA-1234 and allocator PR 987.

Unresolved items to log in postmortem:
- Exact sequence that triggers allocator reroute on transient bind-failure (needs repro).
- Whether soft-affinity causes any measurable degradation for multi-tenant tails (benchmark required).

End of cheatsheet. Keep short, iterate after next incident.
